detailed_rationale:
JM Financial is a diversified financial-services group spanning investment banking/capital markets advisory, wealth management, private markets/asset management, NBFC lending, and affordable home loans (segment mix per FY26: Wealth Management 32%, Private Markets 29%, Corporate Advisory & Capital Markets 21%, Affordable Home Loans 10%, Treasury & Others 6%, Asset Management 1%). On headline valuation this looks cheap -- P/E ~10-11x, price/book ~1.08x -- and our own value score of 89.6 reflects that. But our growth-divergence flag is triggered for good reason: 1-year revenue growth is -6.6% against a 3-year CAGR of +8.7%, i.e., growth has recently reversed, not just decelerated. ROE is mediocre (11.9% latest year, only 8.99% on a 3-year average) for a levered financial-services business (D/E ~1.09), and debtor days have deteriorated from 73.5 to 124 -- a real, measurable signal of either slower collections or softening asset quality in the lending/wealth books, not a rounding change.

Governance history is relevant context: JM Financial and related group entities were subject to a March 2024 SEBI interim order over irregularities in their handling of the Piramal Enterprises NCD public issue (where JM Financial acted as lead manager), followed by a June 2024 administrative warning, and the matter was formally settled in September 2025 (Rs.3.92 Cr settlement, temporary operational restrictions across three group entities). This is now closed rather than an open risk, but it is a real scar on the merchant-banking franchise's recent history and worth noting for completeness rather than treating as fully forgotten. There has also been a recent senior-management departure (SMP resignation, July 2026), which reads as routine rather than alarming on its own.

Reverse-DCF: a 10-11x P/E for a diversified financial with 12% ROE would be reasonable if growth were stable, but the -6.6% 1-year revenue print combined with worsening collections timelines argues the market's caution is earning its keep here -- this looks like a legitimately cheap-for-a-reason situation rather than an unfairly discounted quality franchise.
recommendation_rationale: The quant Sell is well-supported: the growth-divergence flag (3-year +8.7% vs 1-year -6.6%) is a real, recent reversal, not noise, reinforced by materially worsening debtor days and a mediocre 3-year-average ROE (~9%) for a levered balance sheet. The now-settled SEBI matter is a governance scar worth remembering even though resolved. We see the cheap headline multiple as compensation for real, current-period deterioration rather than a mispricing to rescue.
summary: JM Financial is a diversified financial-services group (investment banking, wealth management, NBFC lending, home loans). The stock looks statistically cheap at roughly 10-11 times earnings and about book value, but revenue actually declined 6.6% over the last year (versus 8.7% growth over three years), debtor/collection days have lengthened noticeably, and the group settled a SEBI enforcement matter over a 2024 bond-issue irregularity in September 2025. We read the low valuation as a fair reflection of current business softness rather than an opportunity, and rate this a Sell.
positive_para: The business is genuinely diversified across wealth management, private markets, capital-markets advisory, and lending, with wealth management (32% of the FY26 mix) a scalable, less capital-intensive franchise; the stock trades at only ~10-11x earnings and about 1x book value, and the SEBI enforcement matter from 2024 has been formally settled and closed as of September 2025.
negative_para: Revenue fell 6.6% over the last year even as the 3-year trend was positive -- a genuine, recent reversal our own growth-divergence flag was built to catch -- and debtor days lengthened from 73.5 to 124, a real signal of slower collections or softening asset quality. Return on equity has averaged under 9% over three years for a business carrying meaningful leverage (D/E ~1.09), and the 2024 SEBI action over NCD-issuance irregularities, while settled, is a real governance scar on the merchant-banking franchise.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~10-11x P/E would be attractive for a diversified financial compounding at even high-single-digit growth with a clean 12%+ ROE trend, but the current-year revenue decline and lengthening collection cycle suggest the discount is earned, not a mispricing. Fair-to-cheap on headline multiple, but not a rescue case once the recent deterioration is weighed.
